messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated cluster 'dedicated-3' - tenant 'acme-corp' exceeded latency threshold. p95 >= 1200ms over 5m window, errors increased from 0.2% -> 3.8%. reserved_capacity_utilization: 98%. Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/dedicated-reserved-capacity

pagerduty: PagerDuty INC-2026-0456 triggered for the above alert. Escalation policy: Oncall Eng -> SRE Lead.

Megan L: acked. I'll grab triage. first check: cluster metrics + recent deploys.

Megan L: running quick queries:
```
rcpctl metrics query --cluster dedicated-3 --tenant acme-corp --since 10m --metrics p95_latency,errors,reserved_util
```

Megan L: metrics show p95 1.25s, error spike at 02:18 UTC (connection resets + 429s). reserved units at 98% util and failing to autoscale (scale events show backoff). No new deploys in last hour.

Alex R: seeing a jam in the autoscaler logs: `scale_decision: inhibited due to quota_check=false` — looks like quota check failing because tenant hit reserved limit.

Sam K: immediately bump reserved capacity for acme-corp by 20% (temp) and enable burst mode. This is safer than immediate global throttles. I'll also open a fallback to the cheaper model variant for low priority routes.

Sam K: change I'm about to run:
```bash
internal-api patch /tenants/acme-corp/capacity --body '{"reserved_units_delta": +20, "temporary": true, "ttl_minutes": 60}'
```

Megan L: noted. Before you run it, can we confirm billing/quotas? Priya, FYI for customer comms.

Priya S: noted. I'll prep a short message to Acme support saying we're investigating increased latency and we've temporarily increased capacity. ETA 2h for full postmortem. Do we have numbers on % impacted requests?

Megan L: from logs ~30% of requests in the window saw retries / 429s. Most are lower-priority batch inference. High-priority interactive calls were affected intermittently.

Alex R: applying the capacity bump now (will also kick autoscaler).

Alex R: ```
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.prod/tenants/acme-corp/actions/bump_capacity" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"units":20,"temporary":true,"ttl":3600}'
```

incident-bot: Action recorded: temporary_capacity_bump executed by Alex R at 1768702602.

Megan L: enabling fallback routing for non-critical routes to model-variant: gpt-small-ql. This should reduce per-request GPU time.

Sam K: also lowered per-tenant max_batch_size from 8 -> 4 to reduce tail latency for interactive requests. Rolling now.

Megan L: monitoring dashboards - p95 dropped from 1250ms -> 420ms within 3 minutes of changes. Error rate trending down to 0.9%. reserved_util down to 85% after burst.

Priya S: sent customer update: "We've applied a temporary capacity increase and routing changes; latency reduced. We'll follow up with RCA and next steps."

Megan L: handing off to Sam K for continued monitoring and RCA. I'm going to document steps in the incident ticket and attach snippets.

Sam K: taking over. I'll keep the temporary capacity for 60min and then evaluate rollback. Plan for follow-up: 1) RCA for why autoscaler failed (quota check path), 2) check whether reserved limits should include burst headroom, 3) propose automated fallback policy.

Sam K: created incident ticket: INC-2026-0456 in JIRA (link in incident ticket). Adding checklist: triage notes, mitigations, metrics snapshots, customer comms.

Megan L: quick note — saw ~6k requests queued briefly in front of the model shard at peak, looks like KV cache thrash. Adding to RCA.

Alex R: :thumbsup: good catch.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Pager resolved (auto) at 1768703351. Resolution note: temporary capacity bump + fallback routing restored p95 <= 500ms. Incident remains open for RCA and postmortem.

Priya S: I'll keep Acme updated and share postmortem draft when available.

Sam K: leaving oncall notes in the handoff channel. If p95 climbs again, escalate to infra-ops for a full cluster scale.

Megan L: thanks all — closing Slack triage loop.
